principles: The Bosch color scheme relies on white and black with sparing use of one accent color, creating an open, breathable, reserved impression while leaving room for motif and brand promise.
The colorful narrow Supergraphic provides liveliness and contrast against the reserved overall color impression.
Use one accent color at a time. Accent colors add vibrancy and differentiation without overwhelming the design.
Warning and notification colors have a functional character and are not general decorative design colors.
Gradients are not permitted. Use individual colors or lighter/darker gradations with the main accent color.
Color gradations support accessibility and contrast. The background and text color distance should be at least 50 according to the guidance referenced in the page.
ai_implications: Prefer neutral surfaces and restrained accents. Avoid making color the dominant visual element unless the use case is functional or tied to the Supergraphic.
Use the Supergraphic as a controlled visual contrast element rather than replacing it with broad decorative gradients.
When generating layouts, select one accent family such as Bosch Blue, Purple, Turquoise, or Green for a single composition unless a functional state requires another color.
Reserve yellow, red, green, and blue functional states for warnings, errors, success, important notifications, and information.
Do not create gradient fills from Bosch palette colors. Use discrete swatches, flat fills, or explicit gradation steps.
For text and delicate UI elements, use high-contrast combinations, typically black or white text, and check light/dark theme contrast.

base_colors.name: Bosch Gray 50
base_colors.role: Neutral gray reference in base palette.

brand_color.name: Bosch Red 50
brand_color.rule: Exclusive for the Bosch logotype and error messages when used as functional red. Not for general accent or decorative use.

accent_colors.name: Bosch Purple 40
accent_colors.role: Accent color derived from the Supergraphic.

accent_colors.name: Bosch Blue 50
accent_colors.role: Primary digital accent, links, buttons, information.

accent_colors.name: Bosch Turquoise 50
accent_colors.role: Accent color derived from the Supergraphic.

accent_colors.name: Bosch Green 50
accent_colors.role: Accent color and positive feedback color.

functional_colors.name: Bosch Yellow 85
functional_colors.usage_rule: Use for important notifications and warnings only, not as decorative color.

functional_colors.name: Bosch Green 50
functional_colors.usage_rule: Use for positive feedback, success, or tip states.

functional_colors.name: Bosch Red 50
functional_colors.usage_rule: Use for error messages. Red gradations are restricted to error states.

functional_colors.name: Bosch Blue 50
functional_colors.usage_rule: Use for information and interactive accents.

functional_colors.name: Warning
functional_colors.usage_rule: Used for warning callouts, alert/don't states, and attention surfaces.

functional_colors.name: Note
functional_colors.usage_rule: Used for note callouts or notification emphasis.

functional_colors.name: Info
functional_colors.usage_rule: Used for information callouts and darker blue UI states.

gradation_rules.naming: The numeric suffix indicates brightness. Higher value means lighter color, lower value means darker color.
restrictions: Do not use gradations alone without the main accent color
Prefer black or white font color for contrast
Use red and yellow gradations only for functional states when applicable

light_theme.description: Light Mode is the Bosch default. It uses bright and white backgrounds with selective functional color emphasis.

dark_theme.description: Dark Mode is for screens/UI in night or dark environments. It reverses the color impression: white becomes black, and backgrounds use dark base colors or Bosch Blue below 20.
accent_guidance: Flat elements on dark backgrounds should use the respective accent color
Typefaces and delicate elements on dark backgrounds should use lighter accent gradations
Example: Bosch Blue 50 on white can become Bosch Blue 70 on dark

do: Use white, black, and gray as the foundation of most layouts.
Use Bosch Blue 50 for primary digital interactive elements unless another accent family is explicitly required.
Use one accent family per composition.
Use red only for logotype or error states, depending on context.
Use yellow only for warnings or important notifications.
Use gradations to solve contrast and hierarchy, especially in light/dark themes.
Keep font color black or white unless specific typography guidance allows an exception.
dont: Do not use Bosch Red as a decorative accent.
Do not mix multiple accent colors decoratively in one layout.
Do not treat warning/notification colors as brand decoration.
Do not rely on automatically converted PMS/RAL/NCS/HKS/LAB values without manual verification.
